summary: Build report pages bespoke and with soft-ui, then judge each pair blind for intent match

a_only: Recommendation is 'merge, after a look at R4 and R8', with the reasoning that both drops are smaller than the run-to-run spread and may be noise
Subtitle states the run size: 12 prompts x 4 runs x 6 waves
Dumbbell chart shows baseline-to-candidate movement per item with the +/- spread bars, so you can see each change against its noise
States that the scores settled from wave 3, and that candidate quality moved less than 0.012 over waves 3 to 6
Regressed rows are highlighted and tagged REG in the table and in the chart
Items-improved tile names the two biggest gains (R3 +0.12, R6 +0.15)
b_only: Recommendation is 'Fix those two before you merge', which is a different merge call from A
Items-unchanged tile (2: R2, R7)
Separate grouped bar chart of absolute baseline and candidate scores per item
Separate diverging bar chart of the change per item, sorted by delta
Table sorted with the regressions first, with an inline bar for the candidate score
Spread shown only as two table columns, not in a chart and not tied to the regressions
Delta colours are inverted in the table: negative values are green and positive values are red, which works against the emphasis on the regressions
judge.why: Both pages give the same verdict, KPIs, convergence lines, rubric table and run facts in nearly the same order. A serves the skill author better because it plots each delta against its spread, says plainly when the scores settled, and gives a reasoned merge call, while B gives a different merge call with no reasoning, shows the spread only as table numbers, and colours the deltas the wrong way round.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a verdict banner that gives the recommendation ("merge, after a look at R4 and R8"). Below it are four KPI tiles (quality, stability, items improved, items regressed), then a dumbbell chart of baseline and candidate scores for each rubric item, sorted by change, with spread bars and the R4 and R8 regressions highlighted, next to two wave line charts that answer "did the scores settle". The page ends with a full rubric table and a run-facts list.

tool.friction:
The first render printed "check ok". Five things were hard or missing.
1. Summary tiles from the final wave: no data-driven way to get them. I wanted quality and stability at wave 6, with the delta from the baseline. That needs a filter to the last row and a pivot by version, and the stat `where` and `agg` options do not do this. I typed the values (0.853, +0.052 and so on) by hand, so they are not tied to the data.
2. Improved, unchanged and regressed counts: none of the expression, `where` or `by` options can derive a status column from delta. I typed the counts and the item lists by hand. A conditional computed column, for example `status: "delta > 0 ? 'improved' : ..."`, would fix this. It would also allow `stats: {by: status}` and a tone column in the table.
3. Regression flags: the table cannot mark R4 and R8 (the rows in run.json `regressions`) as bad from a second dataset. A tone map works only on a value in the same row, and the delta of R8 is -0.04, not a category.
4. Column labels: the table shows raw names such as baseline_spread. I could rename them with {key, label}, but that makes the spec longer.
5. Delta-only chart: I was not sure if a negative bar gets a bad colour, or if sort: -y works with fmt: delta.
I could not check the look by eye. I did not open the page.

a_only: A full table of all 12 changes, grouped by intent, with stage and owner filters and days-in-stage bars
A separate Intents table (id, title, status)
A 'changes in flight 12' KPI and an 'intents 3 (2 building, 1 ready)' KPI
A red alert banner that says CH-0029 is stuck, and also calls CH-0021 and CH-0024 stuck for 8 to 9 days in verify (the data marks them not stuck)
An empty DONE column in the pipeline
Question dates as absolute dates (2026-11-26)
b_only: One 'Waits for you' list that merges the stuck change, the 3 questions, and the 2 changes owned by you ('your turn', with the next action)
A 'Slow movers (7+ days in stage)' table with 4 changes, including CH-0026 Dark mode tokens
KPIs for 'changes 7+ days in stage' (4) and 'ready to show / merge' (2)
Question badges (Q-31, Q-32, Q-33) and 'you' badges on the pipeline cards, which tie questions to changes
Intent progress rows with intent titles, status, change, stuck and question counts, and a percent complete
Stage-ordered segments in the intent bars, labelled inline
Relative question ages ('asked 2 days ago')
judge.why: B serves the owner's morning job better: it puts everything that waits for the owner in one list, ties the questions to the pipeline cards, and shows intent progress with titles and a percent. A has the same core views (KPIs, kanban, stacked intent bars, question list) and adds a filterable table, but its stuck banner mislabels slow changes as stuck, and its intent chart shows only IDs, with stages out of pipeline order.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a row of 5 KPI tiles: stuck changes, open questions, changes you own, changes 7+ days in one stage, and changes ready to show. Below the tiles, a "Waits for you" list (stuck item, questions, your turn) sits beside a table of slow movers; then a 5-column pipeline board (planned, tests, build, verify, show) with the stuck card in red, question and owner tags, and amber ages; then one stacked stage bar per intent with a progress percentage.

fixed_lines: fixed layout[0].stats.items[4]: dropped "1 ready" with no value; a comma inside {...} splits the text there. Next time: quote text that has a comma, e.g. sub: "a, b, c"
fixed layout[2].row[1].chart: chart had no `y`; counted rows per x. Next time: y: <column>, or agg: count
tool.friction:
Disclosure: after rendering I opened shot.png in the output folder to check my page. It turned out to show the bespoke page ("ledger · pdlc board"), not mine. I did not change the spec after I saw it, but the comparison for this run may not be fully blind. The render does not say where its own screenshot goes, or whether it makes one. A render flag that writes a screenshot to a named path would stop this mix-up.

Gaps:
(1) No join across datasets. The question list cannot show the title or stage of each question's change, and the board cannot badge a change that has an open question. I put the change id on each question as a badge instead.
(2) No derived per-intent "progress %". A stacked horizontal bar by stage is the closest. A meter per intent would need values that I work out by hand.
(3) No easy way to show "aging" rows (7+ days in stage) as a tone or a highlight. I put them in the callout text and sorted the table by days_in_stage.
(4) The stat tile values (stuck, questions, owned by you) are hand counts. stats by: works on one column, but not on a filter such as owner == you or stuck == true. Each tile needs a where: plus a count.
(5) I was not sure that the board tone {stuck: {true: bad}} matches a JSON boolean. render gave no warning, but I could not check the result without a screenshot of my own page.
(6) A combined "waits for you" list (stuck changes, questions, and changes owned by you in one feed) is not possible from three datasets without a union.

a_only: Pass rate KPI (97.3%) and a stacked status bar under the KPIs
Root-cause callout tells the reader what to fix (price.total expired-code handling) and shows the two-line call path
One suite table holds total time, test count, mean time and fail/flaky counts per suite, with inline bars
Error message and failing test file:line shown inline on each failed row, with the stack trace one click away
Duration of each failed test
Note below the slowest tests that 2 search tests take a third of the suite time
All-tests table opens by default with a name search box and filters for suite and status
b_only: Three separate bar charts: total time by suite, mean test time by suite, and a stacked chart of results by suite
Failed tests grouped under suite headings with counts
Total-time KPI and total-tests KPI as cards
Slowest-tests table shows the status of each test, has inline bars, and is paged over all 271 tests
All-tests table folded by default, grouped by suite
judge.why: Both pages follow the brief's order: verdict callout, KPIs, suite timing, then failed and flaky tests. A serves the on-call engineer better: each failed row shows its error and file:line, and the callout names the fix. In B, every failure card is folded, so the reader must click seven cards to see any error, and the slowest tests come after the failures.

bespoke.notes: The page follows the reader's order. It starts with a "build failed" header, status KPI tiles and a stacked status bar. Next is a callout that names the shared root cause of all 7 failures (app/cart/price.py:52 raises ValueError: code expired). Below that, a suites-by-duration bar table sits beside a slowest-tests table. Then come the failed-tests table, with each error and an expandable stack trace, and the flaky-tests table. Last is a filterable table of all 271 tests. The page embeds its data and uses no libraries. The first screenshot showed an error: a global const named "top" clashed with window.top. I renamed it, and the second screenshot rendered correctly.

tool.friction:
The first render printed "check ok", with no fixed or error lines. Five things were hard or missing.
1. Data is not joined. The tool cannot join failures.json (error and trace) to results.csv (status, ms, retries). The failed-tests list therefore has no duration or retry count, and the flaky tests have no errors to show. The flaky table shows only suite, test, ms and retries.
2. The summary is typed by hand. The page cannot compute the "build failed" verdict or the shared root cause (all 7 traces end in app/cart/price.py:52, ValueError('code expired')). I checked the data with Python and then wrote the callout text and the subtitle counts myself. A "group by error" or "group by last trace line" option, or a derived column for the list, would make the common cause visible without hand-written text.
3. Top-N is not clear. `limit` on a table means "rows per page", so the "Slowest tests" table pages through all rows. It does not show only the top 10. A top-N option for tables, like `limit` on chart, would help.
4. Totals are raw. The "Total time" stat sums ms and shows it in ms. The fmt `s` is not available on stat, so the large number is not converted to seconds.
5. Paths are long. Data paths from the output folder need `../../../reports/...`, which was easy to get right but verbose. No other confusion: catalog plus explain was enough to write the spec in one pass.

a_only: Multi-series line chart of lines changed each week for each file (10 overlapping lines)
Weekly detail table, grouped by file and filterable, with the lines and commits for each file in each week
KPI note '84 days with commits'
KPI 'Top 2 files share 50%' (B reports 77% in 4 files instead)
Heatmap used as the 'change together' view, with column totals for each week
Recommendation of one Engine wall for the tax and discount rules, with invoice.py as the Manager that calls it
b_only: Pairwise correlation matrix of weekly churn: a real 'which files change together' view with values such as invoice/models 0.75 and invoice/emails 0.72
Recommendation of two walls: a Rules engine (vat, discount, tax) and an Invoice workflow (invoice with models and emails), plus 'leave the other 6 files as they are'
Bars coloured by wall assignment (rules engine, invoice workflow, calm), with the commit count on each label
Heatmap peak W41-W42 marked, with values printed on the hottest cells
Daily commits chart with the busy period (29 Sep to 19 Oct) shaded and the peak day (19 Oct, 14 commits) called out
'Active weeks' column (for example 12/12) and a named wall for each file in the hot-spot table
Share of lines held by the rules files (63%)
judge.why: B answers the architect's three questions directly: a co-change correlation matrix shows which files change together, and the bars, heatmap and table all carry the same wall assignment. A has the same core views (KPIs, callout, ranked bars, file-by-week heatmap, daily commits, hot-spot table), but it uses the heatmap as a stand-in for co-change, adds a noisy line chart and a very long detail table, and reaches a different and weaker wall recommendation.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a row of KPI tiles and a recommendation box. The box proposes a rules-engine wall around vat.py, discount.py and tax.py, which hold 63% of changed lines, and an invoice-workflow wall around invoice.py. Below the box are four views: a bar chart that ranks files by lines changed, a file-by-week heatmap that marks the W41 to W42 peak, a chart of commits each day with the busy period shaded, and a co-change correlation matrix shown beside a hot spot table. Each view uses the same hot, warm and calm colours, and each chart is hand-built inline SVG with no libraries.

fixed_lines: fixed layout[0].stats.items[0]: dropped "12 weeks" with no value; a comma inside {...} splits the text there. Next time: quote text that has a comma, e.g. sub: "a, b, c"
tool.friction: The table cannot aggregate. I wanted a hot-spot table with one row per file (total lines, total commits, share of churn). To get it, I computed the totals by hand and put them inline as a CSV dataset. The spec repeats derived numbers, and they do not follow filters. A table option such as `agg`, or computed data with group-by (for example `data: {file: churn.csv, group: file, sum: [lines, commits]}`), would remove that step. The stat tiles have the same problem: total lines (5681), the top-2 share (50%) and the peak week (890) are numbers I worked out myself. I could have computed total lines with stat data+agg, but no option gives a share of the total or the max of a group sum. There is also no co-change component. The brief asks which files "change together", and the data has no file-pair co-commit counts. So I used a file x week heatmap as a stand-in. A co-change matrix (file x file, from shared weeks or commits) would show coupling directly. The line chart with 10 file series is probably busy. A 'top N series, others grouped' option would help. Data paths had to climb out of the run folder (../../../reports/R7-churn/). That worked, but it was not obvious from the docs that a path with .. is allowed. The only fix was a comma inside an unquoted flow-map value, and the "Next time" hint made it clear.
